subject: Cross-border transfer evidence & service-provider delegation under CCPA/CPRA
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@brightleaf.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Privacy Team <privacy@brightleaf.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence for cross-border transfers + confirmation of service-provider handling

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our pre-contract checklist we need two things clarified for CCPA/CPRA: (1) a list of all subprocessors that may access or process California-resident personal data and their country of processing, and (2) an explanation of how Redwood will meet the "service provider" restrictions (limited use/ no sale), including any onshore fallback options if offshore subprocessors are unavailable during an incident.

Specifically, BrightLeaf asks for:
- A CSV with current subprocessors (name, role, primary country, data categories).
- A copy of the DPA exhibit language you propose for CPRA/CCPA service provider commitments.
- Evidence that telemetry/telemetry exports are handled in a way consistent with SP boundaries (logs retention, aggregate-only exports).

Can you get this over by EOD Wednesday (2027-06-16)? If you need to flag anything operationally impossible, call that out — our security team will triage.

Appreciate it,
Samantha
Privacy Manager, BrightLeaf Therapeutics
privacy@brightleaf.com

Attachments: none

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evidence for cross-border transfers + confirmation of service-provider handling

Team — forwarding BrightLeaf's request. Key asks: subprocessors CSV, DPA exhibit for CPRA/CCPA that explicitly calls us a service provider (limited use/no sale), and a short write-up on telemetry/exports and any onshore fallback commitments we can support.

Notes / constraints we should surface if applicable:
- We have a mix of cloud-managed SaaS providers and partner hosting locations; some telemetry aggregation uses EU-based analytics — need to confirm whether any raw CA-resident PII crosses borders.
- Onshore fallback: we can offer an onshore GPU fallback pool (Dedicated) but it requires lead time to curate keys and routing; not all customers buy Dedicated.

Marissa — can you compile the subprocessors CSV and draft the DPA exhibit language?
Jonas — can you comment on the legal wording re: "sale"/limited use and add any redlines for novel onshore fallback commitments?
Laura — can you confirm from infra whether any telemetry exports contain user identifiers and whether a short-term onshore export option exists?

Target: get a package ready to send to BrightLeaf by EOD Wednesday to meet their internal review.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Customer Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evidence for cross-border transfers + confirmation of service-provider handling

Diego —

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20270614.csv (sample rows below), plus a draft DPA exhibit that maps CPRA service-provider language into our standard exhibit. I also included a simple diagram (crossborder_flow.drawio.png) showing routing and fallback.

Sample CSV rows:
name,role,primary_country,data_categories
CloudStorageCo,object-storage,us,customer_files;logs
EU-Analytics,analytics,ie,aggregated_telemetry
ManagedCacheLtd,cache,gb,kv-cache

Draft exhibit highlights (summary):
- Redwood confirms it will act as a "Service Provider" as defined under the CCPA/CPRA and will not sell personal information; usage limited to providing services under the agreement.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide prior notice for new subprocessors and maintain an up-to-date list; subprocessors are bound by equivalent contractual protections.
- Onshore fallback: Redwood offers an onshore processing option (Dedicated or Private deployment) as a contractual add-on. For Hosted customers, in the event of onshore unavailability we commit to (i) encrypt-in-transit and at-rest; (ii) route telemetry aggregations only as aggregate metrics; (iii) provide export of relevant logs within 72 hours to a US-based endpoint.

Questions/asks for review:
- Jonas: the phrase "we commit to provide export of relevant logs within 72 hours" — legal may want to limit SLA/penalty exposure. Suggest either making this a best-effort support or referencing an addendum with explicit SLAs.
- Laura: can you confirm whether the 72-hour export is technically feasible for hosted customers and if there are edge cases where customer data may have crossed borders via analytics pipelines?

If you all sign off I'll package the CSV + DPA exhibit and send to BrightLeaf.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_20270614.csv (spreadsheet stub, 3 rows sample)
- dpa_exhibit_sp_cpra_draft.pdf (redline/summary)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@brightleaf.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Privacy Team <privacy@brightleaf.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for cross-border transfers + confirmation of service-provider handling

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find the requested materials attached: the subprocessors CSV, our proposed DPA exhibit language for CPRA/CCPA service-provider commitments, and a simple routing/fallback diagram. Highlights below: 

1) Subprocessors (CSV): includes current third parties that may process telemetry, caching, or storage. We mark primary country and data categories; note that EU-Analytics only receives aggregated telemetry and is contractually prohibited from re-identifying PII.

2) Exhibit language (attached draft): we explicitly accept "Service Provider" status and commit to "limited use" consistent with CPRA/CCPA. Where customers require an onshore-only processing guarantee, we offer Dedicated or Private deployment add-ons (contractual charge applies).

3) Onshore fallback / exports: for Hosted customers we offer a documented support path — in an incident we'll (A) preserve encrypted backups; (B) export requested logs/data to a US-based endpoint within 72 hours (operational caveats noted in the exhibit); or (C) recommend a migration to Dedicated/Private for long-term onshore requirements. Jonas has added a proposed legal caveat to keep the 72-hour export as a "commercially reasonable" support commitment rather than a hard SLA — happy to surface the exact wording if you prefer firm SLA language.

Next steps: any clarifying questions? If BrightLeaf wants a firm SLA around export timelines or explicit penalties, we should loop in Sales/Revenue to scope costs for Dedicated capacity or a compliance add-on. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the diagram and the exhibit.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Customer Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_20270614.csv (attached)
- dpa_exhibit_sp_cpra_draft.pdf (attached)
- crossborder_flow.drawio.png (attached)
